item.title: Chart Rewind: In 2016, Dierks Bentley’s ‘Black’ Eyed No. 1 on Top Country Albums
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to our podcast, where we dive into the latest trends and hits in the music world. Today, we're shining the spotlight on country music star Dierks Bentley.
[Music transitions to a country tune]
Host: You might know that Dierks Bentley's album "Black" was inspired by his wife, Cassidy, and her maiden name. But did you know that this album was a huge success, topping Billboard's Top Country Albums chart in its first week, back in June 2016? This was actually Bentley's sixth time reaching the top spot on this chart.
[Music transitions to a clip of "Somewhere on a Beach"]
Host: The album "Black" explored themes of love, sex, and relationships, with hit singles like "Somewhere on a Beach", which stayed at number one on Hot Country Songs for three weeks. The album also featured collaborations with notable artists like Elle King, Maren Morris, and Trombone Shorty.
[Music transitions to a clip of "Different for Girls"]
Host: Some of the other notable tracks from the album include "Different for Girls" with Elle King, and the title track "Black", which peaked at number four on the charts. The album was a commercial success, earning a Gold certification from the RIAA in 2017, and later being elevated to Platinum status in 2022.
[Music transitions to a clip of "I'll Be the Moon"]
Host: Dierks Bentley has had an impressive run on the Top Country Albums chart, with his first number one album being "Modern Day Drifter" back in 2005, and his most recent one being "The Mountain" in 2018.
[Outro music plays]
Host: That's all for today's episode. Thanks for tuning in, and we'll catch you on the next one!
